title: Redwood discovery: model selection - Archipelago AI
summary: Intro discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual customer-facing agents. Discussed context length needs (32k vs 100k), tool-calling and function-calling, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, security docs, and schedule technical deep dive + trial cluster for model comparison.
action_items: Jordan Kim: Send model perf spreadsheet comparing Llama-3 / Mistral / Falcon on Archipelago sample workload (due: 2026-12-16)
Priya Shah: Prepare Dedicated trial config and estimated cost for 10k qps baseline (due: 2026-12-18)
Evan Zhou: Share customer security checklist and questions for Redwood (due: 2026-12-15)
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed benchmarks and quantization recommendations
Share SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration guide
Schedule a technical deep dive with infra + security next week
Provision Dedicated trial cluster and run 48h model comparison
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Archipelago Head of ML), Sofia (Eng Mgr), Evan (Security)

00:00 Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Priya is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Liam: Good, thanks. Sorry we ran a little late.
00:10 Jordan: No worries. Quick agenda — we want to understand your workload, constraints, and then talk model selection: open models, context length, multilingual needs, and tool-calling. Then we'll cover deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) given your security requirements. Sound good?
00:25 Sofia: Yep, that works.
00:27 Priya: Great. Liam, can you kick off with a brief on what you're building and the expected usage patterns?
00:33 Liam: Sure. So Archipelago builds a conversational assistant that augments customer support agents across EMEA and APAC. It's multi-lingual — English, Spanish, Japanese — and we'll have mixed workloads: short queries and long context summarization. The big ask is sometimes we need 50k to 100k token context for full conversation histories and long docs, like legal or policy docs. Average concurrent users maybe a few thousand, peak bursts during product launches.
00:59 Jordan: Got it. So long-context support is important. Are you currently using any models or self-hosting?
01:04 Liam: Right now it's prototype on-host via a small fleet on Replicate and some OpenAI calls for stuff that requires tool-calling. Costs are getting crazy with OpenAI, and latency is variable. We want to evaluate open models for cost predictability and to comply with data residency.
01:19 Priya: When you say tool-calling, is that function calls to internal APIs or more like retrieval-augmented generation with tools?
01:25 Liam: Both. We need function-calling for account lookups and also safe tool invocation with audit logs. Security is a must.
01:31 Evan: To expand: we'll need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs for all calls, and KMS integration for encrypting keys. Also EU data residency for EU customers. So Private or Dedicated are interesting. Hosted is okay for lower-sensitivity flows, but we need options.
01:46 Jordan: That's helpful. Priya, can you run through how Redwood supports long context and tool-calling?
01:50 Priya: Sure. So Redwood's runtime supports model variants with extended context lengths — we have verified setups for 32k and 100k contexts depending on the model. The tradeoff is throughput and cost; longer context can increase memory and latency. For tool-calling we support structured function calling and streaming of partial responses. There can be mis-transcriptions — sorry — the integrations let you instrument calls so they show up in audit logs and we can route sensitive flows to Dedicated or Private.
02:18 Liam: Is the 100k context available on open models like Llama-3 or Mistral?
02:22 Priya: Good question. Model support varies. Llama-3 chat variants can be compiled to support large contexts up to 100k in some tuned setups; Mistral has emerging long-context forks (we've worked with Mistral for 64k-type contexts), and for extreme contexts we sometimes do a hybrid: prefix caching, chunked retrieval, or retrieval+RAG to avoid sending entire docs. Also quantization and custom kernels affect memory.
02:43 Sofia: We have heavy multilingual needs. Any models you'd recommend for Japanese plus Spanish support?
02:48 Priya: Llama-3 has decent multi-lingual coverage; Mistral also performs well for European languages; for Japanese we typically test Mistral and some community Japanese-tuned models. We often run a small eval suite on your language sets — compare perplexity and pragmatic downstream metrics — because raw benchmarks don't always capture L2 performance.
03:07 Liam: Are there differences in function-calling or tool-calling between models? Like some models better at following structured function specs?
03:12 Priya: Yes. For example, Llama-3 chat-optimized variants are better at adhering to function schemas out-of-the-box; some Mistral and Falcon chat variants require instruction tuning or light prompting templates to be as consistent. Redwood offers tool-calling shim that translates model output into structured function calls and validates them before calling your API. We also provide retriable fallbacks and validation for safety.
03:33 Evan: On the security front — you mentioned audit logs. Are logs stored in Redwood by default or can they be forwarded to our SIEM?
03:39 Jordan: We have both options. For Hosted, logs are stored in Redwood with retention controls; you can configure exports to your SIEM (S3, syslog). For Dedicated and Private, customers typically route logs directly to their logging infrastructure, and for Private the control plane can be behind your VPC so nothing leaves your network unless you configure it.
03:56 Evan: And KMS?
03:58 Priya: KMS/HSM integrations are supported — both cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and bring-your-own HSM in Private deployments. Keys can be managed by you; Redwood will integrate with envelope encryption so we don't have direct plaintext access.
04:11 Liam: Cost — can you ballpark cost differences between Hosted open-models vs Dedicated?
04:16 Jordan: Ballpark: Hosted open-model usage is pay-as-you-go; costs depend on tokens and model size. Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU capacity — better for high steady volume. For your workload, with long context and multi-lingual, Dedicated could reduce per-token costs if you commit. Priya will prepare a sample cost sheet.
04:34 Priya: We'll run a cost model for a few candidate models: Llama-3 chat (70B), Mistral-chat 7B/30B, Falcon-180B variants if you want; we'll include quantized variants (int8/4) and throughput/latency estimates.
04:51 Sofia: Speaking of quantization — are there issues with hallucination or accuracy when doing int8?
04:56 Priya: Generally, int8/4 quantization can slightly affect generation fidelity, especially for edge-case prompts. We recommend running your eval sets; sometimes we keep the last few layers in higher precision for critical tasks. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on which layers to keep fp16 versus int8 based on your workloads.
05:14 Liam: For tool-calling reliability, we need deterministic outputs for our downstream processors. How do you handle consistency?
05:20 Priya: We support temperature controls, sampling seeds, and deterministic sampling modes for model variants that support them. Also we recommend function-calling schemas and pre-parse validators; the runtime can automatically retry or route to a more deterministic model if the output doesn't match schema.
05:35 Jordan: Any hard constraints around latency SLOs? You mentioned bursts — what's your 95th p99 goals?
05:40 Liam: For interactive agent flows, p95 under 400ms is ideal for short queries; for long-document summarization we accept higher latency (2-5s).
05:50 Priya: That lines up with our Dedicated offering where we tune batch sizes and use low-latency kernels. For hosted we have latency tiers and can prioritize low-latency routes, but Dedicated gives more predictable p95/p99.
06:03 Evan: For data residency — can we keep EU traffic in EU and US in US?
06:07 Jordan: Yes, region routing by policy is supported; we can ensure requests from EU customers stay in EU regions, and for Dedicated/Private you can further restrict.
06:15 Liam: About evaluation — what's a typical benchmarking approach?
06:18 Priya: We take a few steps: you give sample prompts and datasets per language and task; we run automated evals for latency, token cost, output quality (ROUGE, BLEU where applicable), and run human-in-the-loop checks for hallucinations and safety. We also do a 48-hour live-run if you want to test reliability under load.
06:36 Liam: That sounds good. Could you also include function-calling reliability in the bench? Like schema adherence rates?
06:40 Priya: Absolutely. We instrument schema parse success, fallback rates, and end-to-end latency including downstream call time.
06:47 Sofia: Any blockers for us to try Dedicated? Is there a big onboarding overhead?
06:52 Jordan: There's an onboarding checklist but it's straightforward: contract for reserved capacity, basic network setup (VPC peering or private connectivity), SSO, and access controls. Priya will share a template. For Private (on-prem) it's more involved — install and ops but gives full control.
07:08 Evan: One quick thing — for compliance, do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation?
07:11 Jordan: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates; we'll share the docs.
07:15 Evan: And penetration testing reports?
07:17 Jordan: We have summary reports and can sign additional NDAs to share more.
07:21 Liam: Let's talk model candidates now — what would you recommend we start with for our mixed workloads?
07:26 Priya: My recommended shortlist: Llama-3 chat-70B (good chat instruction following and long-context on tuned variants), Mistral-chat-30B (cost-effective and strong European language support), and a quantized Falcon or community 40-70B variant if you need cost-down. We'll run each with your multilingual prompts and function-calling tests. For extreme 100k context use-cases we might use a Llama-3 tuned variant or a chunked RAG pattern.
07:52 Liam: Any concern about hallucinations with Llama-3 at long context lengths?
07:55 Priya: Hallucination risk increases with length if you don't use retrieval and grounding. Our recommendations: use retrieval-augmented steps, prefix/KV caching for repeated conversation history, and prompt engineering. We'll include failure cases in the benchmark report.
08:08 Jordan: Quick logistics — Priya will own the trial provisioning and benchmarks, Jordan will own commercial and next meeting. Evan you'll own the security checklist. Sound right?
08:17 Evan: Yep.
08:19 Liam: Yep.
08:20 Jordan: Great — we'll recap next steps.
08:23 [auto-generated summary appears — may be imperfect] Summary: Discussed multi-lingual assistant needs; agreed shortlist Llama-3 / Mistral / Falcon variants; prioritized Dedicated trial for cost predictability and compliance. Action items recorded.
08:35 Sofia: One more question — tool-calling with external APIs — can Redwood enforce rate limits or apply per-tenant quotas?
08:40 Priya: Yes, you can configure per-route quotas and rate limits, and Redwood's routing policies can throttle or circuit-break to protect downstream services.
08:50 Liam: Ok, let's wrap with concrete next steps — timeline?
08:53 Jordan: We'll target sending the benchmark plan and security docs by EOD Thursday (that's 2026-12-16). Priya will provision a Dedicated trial environment by Friday the 18th. We'll schedule a technical deep dive for next week — how's Tuesday 11am UTC?
09:07 Liam: That works.
09:09 Evan: Works for me.
09:11 Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links to the bench plan and a calendar invite.
09:16 Sofia: Thanks all.
09:18 [call ends]
